name: United States
note: The United States in the style of the Russian model tree. The administrations branch follows the real laws of 2001-2022 on their dates; the political branch has the two-party system (the historical path) and third-party turns that bring to power only real parties of the data (Libertarian, Green, Reform, Constitution) plus a military junta; alternatives are a counterfactual, not a claim about the parties. Economy, military, foreign policy and society branches build, fix the starting spirits (data/spirits/usa.json), unlock decisions (data/decisions/usa.json) and grant research. Policies named after real laws are cited; effects are gameplay estimates. Wars stay in the scripted conflict events.

focuses.name: A new administration
focuses.description: Set the priorities of the administration for its first term.

focuses.name: Economic growth and tax relief
focuses.description: Pass the tax cuts the President campaigned on. The Economic Growth and Tax Relief Reconciliation Act was signed on 7 June 2001.

focuses.name: No Child Left Behind
focuses.description: Pass a national education bill that ties federal school funding to state standards and testing. The No Child Left Behind Act became law in 2002.

focuses.name: Medicare prescription drug benefit
focuses.description: Add prescription drug cover to Medicare. The Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act was signed on 8 December 2003.

focuses.name: The PATRIOT Act
focuses.description: Expand surveillance powers and information sharing between agencies after the September 11 attacks, as the USA PATRIOT Act did in 2001.

focuses.name: Department of Homeland Security
focuses.description: Create a cabinet department for domestic security. The Homeland Security Act was enacted on 25 November 2002.

focuses.name: Rescue the banks
focuses.description: The Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 3 October 2008 creates the $700 billion Troubled Asset Relief Program.

focuses.name: Protect the Social Security surplus
focuses.description: Dedicate the Social Security surplus to Social Security and paying down the national debt, as the 2000 Gore campaign proposed.

focuses.name: Targeted tax cuts
focuses.description: Pass targeted tax cuts for child care, higher education, health insurance and long-term care, as the 2000 Gore campaign proposed.

focuses.name: Health, education and environment trust funds
focuses.description: Create the three trust funds for health care, education and the environment proposed by the 2000 Gore campaign.

focuses.name: Republican legislative agenda
focuses.description: Use the position of the party in government to pass its programme.

focuses.name: Democratic legislative agenda
focuses.description: Use the position of the party in government to pass its programme.

focuses.name: Bipartisan compromise
focuses.description: Seek votes across the aisle for major bills.

focuses.name: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act
focuses.description: A stimulus of about $787 billion against the Great Recession, signed in February 2009.

focuses.name: Affordable Care Act
focuses.description: Expand health coverage with subsidised insurance, signed on 23 March 2010; its major provisions took effect in 2014.

focuses.name: Dodd–Frank financial reform
focuses.description: New rules for Wall Street and a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, signed on 21 July 2010.

focuses.name: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
focuses.description: Cut corporate and individual tax rates and raise the standard deduction, signed on 22 December 2017.

focuses.name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
focuses.description: Federal money for roads, bridges, transit and rail, signed on 15 November 2021.

focuses.name: CHIPS and Science Act
focuses.description: About $52.7 billion for semiconductor plants and research, signed on 9 August 2022.

focuses.name: Inflation Reduction Act
focuses.description: Energy investment, lower drug prices and deficit reduction, signed on 16 August 2022.

focuses.name: The future of American politics
focuses.description: Whether the two-party system holds or a third force breaks through.

focuses.name: The two-party system
focuses.description: Democrats and Republicans alternate in power. This is the path the United States took.

focuses.name: A libertarian moment
focuses.description: Voters tired of both parties turn to the Libertarian Party.

focuses.name: A Libertarian administration
focuses.description: The Libertarian Party takes the White House.

focuses.name: Small government
focuses.description: Cut agencies and regulations; bring troops home.

focuses.name: A green wave
focuses.description: Climate and inequality bring voters to the Greens.

focuses.name: A Green administration
focuses.description: The Green Party takes the White House.

focuses.name: A green industrial programme
focuses.description: Wind, solar and rail across the country.

focuses.name: A populist revolt
focuses.description: Anger at trade deals and elites lifts the Reform Party.

focuses.name: A Reform administration
focuses.description: The most popular nationalist party takes the White House.

focuses.name: A tariff wall
focuses.description: High tariffs to bring factories home.

focuses.name: A religious right
focuses.description: Christian conservatives leave the Republicans for the Constitution Party.

focuses.name: A Constitution Party administration
focuses.description: The most popular religious party takes the White House.

focuses.name: The army steps in
focuses.description: With the republic in crisis, the generals prepare to take over.

focuses.name: Military council
focuses.description: The armed forces remove the government. The coup may fail.

focuses.name: Return to the barracks
focuses.description: The council hands power back to an elected government.

focuses.name: Economic agenda
focuses.description: Set the economic priorities of the administration.

focuses.name: After the dot-com crash
focuses.description: Let the bubble deflate and support the recovery.

focuses.name: Trade agenda
focuses.description: Negotiate new trade agreements.

focuses.name: National energy policy
focuses.description: Set a national energy strategy.

focuses.name: Homeownership
focuses.description: Encourage home buying with cheap credit.

focuses.name: Silicon Valley
focuses.description: Support for software, cloud and the internet economy.

focuses.name: Shale oil and gas
focuses.description: Horizontal drilling and fracking open new fields in Texas, North Dakota and Pennsylvania.

focuses.name: Gulf Coast refining
focuses.description: Expand the refineries and petrochemical plants of the Gulf Coast.

focuses.name: Gas exports
focuses.description: Liquefied gas terminals for exports to Europe and Asia.

focuses.name: United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement
focuses.description: A new trade agreement replacing NAFTA, in force from 1 July 2020.

focuses.name: Manufacturing renewal
focuses.description: Bring factories back to the Midwest.

focuses.name: Housing finance
focuses.description: Mortgage lending and home building grow fast.

focuses.name: Commercial space
focuses.description: Contracts for private launch companies.

focuses.name: Clean energy
focuses.description: Tax credits for wind, solar and batteries.

focuses.name: Semiconductors
focuses.description: New chip plants at home.

focuses.name: Artificial intelligence
focuses.description: Data centres and research for artificial intelligence.

focuses.name: Modernise the grid
focuses.description: Transmission lines and storage for a modern grid.

focuses.name: Quadrennial defence review
focuses.description: Review strategy, forces and budgets.

focuses.name: Missile defence
focuses.description: Fund national missile defence programmes.

focuses.name: Force transformation
focuses.description: Restructure the armed forces around lighter, networked units.

focuses.name: Carrier fleet
focuses.description: New aircraft carriers and naval bases.

focuses.name: Special operations
focuses.description: Expand Special Operations Command for counter-terrorism.

focuses.name: Armed drones
focuses.description: Armed drones for surveillance and strikes.

focuses.name: Defence industry
focuses.description: Expand the arms plants and ammunition production.

focuses.name: The surge in Iraq
focuses.description: More than 20,000 additional troops, mostly to Baghdad, announced in January 2007.

focuses.name: Cyber command
focuses.description: A command for cyber operations.

focuses.name: Global basing
focuses.description: Air bases and ports for global reach.

focuses.name: Withdrawal from Iraq
focuses.description: Bring the troops home from Iraq; the withdrawal was mostly completed by December 2011.

focuses.name: Operation Inherent Resolve
focuses.description: Lead the international coalition against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria from 15 June 2014.

focuses.name: United States Space Force
focuses.description: A space service branch of the armed forces, established on 20 December 2019.

focuses.name: Withdrawal from Afghanistan
focuses.description: Withdraw from Afghanistan; the Department of Defense completed the withdrawal on 30 August 2021.

focuses.name: Great-power competition
focuses.description: Rebuild forces for competition with China and Russia.

focuses.description: Set the course of American foreign policy.

focuses.name: A coalition against terrorism
focuses.description: Build an international coalition after the September 11 attacks.

focuses.name: NATO enlargement
focuses.description: Support NATO membership for the democracies of Central and Eastern Europe.

focuses.name: Free trade partners
focuses.description: Trade agreements with allies in Asia and the Americas.

focuses.name: New START

focuses.name: Partnership with Israel
focuses.description: Military aid and diplomatic support for Israel.

focuses.name: Pivot to Asia
focuses.description: Shift forces and diplomacy toward the Asia-Pacific.

focuses.name: Sanctions on Russia

focuses.name: Indo-Pacific partners
focuses.description: Closer ties with India, Japan and Australia.

focuses.name: Security assistance for Ukraine

focuses.name: Rally the allies
focuses.description: Unite NATO and the G7 behind common aims.

focuses.name: Technology export controls
focuses.description: Restrict exports of advanced chips to rivals.

focuses.name: Domestic agenda
focuses.description: Priorities at home: schools, health and science.

focuses.name: Federal research funding
focuses.description: More money for national laboratories and universities.

focuses.name: Community colleges
focuses.description: Job training at community colleges.

focuses.name: Broadband for rural America
focuses.description: High-speed internet in the countryside.

focuses.name: Medical research
focuses.description: Double funding for medical research.

focuses.name: Water and transit

focuses.name: Army modernisation

focuses.name: Medium brigades

focuses.name: The National Guard

focuses.name: Fifth-generation fighters

focuses.name: Hypersonic weapons
focuses.description: Research into hypersonic missiles and defences.

focuses.name: Shipbuilding
focuses.description: Expand the naval shipyards.

focuses.name: Partners in Africa

focuses.name: Partners in the Americas
focuses.description: Trade, aid and security cooperation in Latin America.

focuses.name: G20 leaders' summits

focuses.name: Diplomacy on Korea

focuses.name: Climate diplomacy
